# The contract the verifier MUST establish, and the tool-independent
# mechanism by which each predicate is decided.
The canonical LOGICAL symbol is:
BootstrapValidPostControlFlowToken
Its OBJECT-FORMAT SPELLING is resolved from the target object format:
Mach-O  -> _BootstrapValidPostControlFlowToken   (leading underscore)
ELF    ->  BootstrapValidPostControlFlowToken   (no prefix)
The spelling is NEVER guessed from the host. It is passed explicitly
from src/CMakeLists.txt as CONTROL_FLOW_TOKEN_TARGET_OBJECT_FORMAT
---- The tool-independent symbol-identity mechanism ------------------
# Both Apple nm and GNU nm support the SAME two flags with the SAME
# meaning, which is what makes the check portable:
#   nm --format=posix --no-weak <object>
# --format=posix  -> "<name> <type> <value> <size>" with an
#                    UNAMBIGUOUS type letter, one record per symbol.
# --no-weak       -> weak definitions are OMITTED entirely.
# Observed type letters (measured on BOTH platforms, see below):
#   global strong text   T
#   weak text            W      (removed by --no-weak)
#   undefined            U
#   local text           t
#   common               C      (removed by --no-weak)
# WHY --no-weak IS LOAD-BEARING (measured, not assumed):
#   On ELF, GNU nm reports a weak definition as "W" and the plain
#   type letter alone would reject it.
#   On Mach-O, the DEFAULT nm reports a weak definition as "T" -- the
#   SAME letter as a strong definition. The type letter alone is
#   therefore NOT sufficient on Mach-O.
#   With --no-weak, the weak Mach-O definition is filtered out and the
#   symbol disappears from the output entirely, so it can be
#   distinguished from a strong definition.
# A weak definition is not a harmless near-miss: it LINKS. Measured:
#   an object whose only definition of the symbol is weak satisfies a
#   reference to it at link time (LINK_RC=0). So a verifier that
#   accepts it would admit an object with no strong production
#   authority.
SYMBOL_NAME_EXACT         = YES   the record name equals the target-format spelling EXACTLY
SYMBOL_IS_DEFINED        = YES   the type is a DEFINITION (T), not U
SYMBOL_IS_GLOBAL         = YES   the type letter is UPPERCASE (global), not lowercase (local)
SYMBOL_IS_CODE           = YES   the type letter is T (text/code), not D/B/R/S/N etc.
SYMBOL_IS_STRONG         = YES   the record survived --no-weak, i.e. it is not weak/common
SYMBOL_DEFINITION_COUNT  = 1    exactly one matching definition record
OBJECT_NONEMPTY          = YES   the file has a nonzero size
NM_EXECUTION_SUCCESSFUL  = YES   nm exited 0
REJECT_UNDEFINED_SYMBOL          the only match is type U
REJECT_LOCAL_SYMBOL              the only match is a lowercase (local) type
REJECT_SYMBOL_NAME_MISMATCH      no record with the EXACT target-format name
REJECT_DUPLICATE_DEFINITION      more than one matching definition
REJECT_INVALID_OBJECT            the file is missing, empty, or not a readable object
REJECT_UNSUPPORTED_OBJECT_FORMAT the target object format is neither Mach-O nor ELF
REJECT_NM_FAILURE                nm was missing or exited nonzero
REJECT_WEAK_SYMBOL               the only match was a weak/common definition

CONTROL_FLOW_TOKEN_OBJECT_STATUS=PASS
